topics.title: Understanding Hindi Sentence Structure
topics.description: Learn the foundational Subject + Object + Verb (SOV) order in Hindi.

lesson.introduction: Unlike English, which uses a Subject + Verb + Object (SVO) word order, Hindi follows a Subject + Object + Verb (SOV) structure. The action verb always comes at the very end of the sentence.

points.title: Basic SOV Order
points.description: In Hindi, the object comes before the verb. For example, 'I apple eat' instead of 'I eat an apple'.

questions.question: What is the basic word order of a standard Hindi sentence?
questions.explanation: Hindi follows the SOV (Subject + Object + Verb) sentence structure.

questions.question: Complete the sentence structure pattern in Hindi: Subject + ______ + Verb.
questions.explanation: The object sits between the subject and the final verb.

questions.question: Where does the action verb appear in a basic Hindi sentence?
questions.explanation: In Hindi SOV structure, the verb always concludes the sentence.

questions.question: Complete: Main seb ___ hoon. (eat)
questions.explanation: Khata/Khaati represents the verb placed at the end before the helping verb.

topics.title: Personal Pronouns
topics.description: Learn core personal pronouns in Hindi including formal and informal forms of 'you'.

lesson.introduction: Personal pronouns are essential for identifying who is performing an action. Hindi features multiple levels of 'you' depending on social hierarchy and respect.

points.title: Primary Pronouns
points.description: Core singular and plural pronouns for everyday speech.

questions.question: Which pronoun means 'I' in Hindi?
questions.explanation: Main (मैं) is the first-person singular pronoun meaning 'I'.

questions.question: The formal and respectful word for 'You' in Hindi is ___.
questions.explanation: Aap (आप) is used for elders, seniors, and formal acquaintances.

questions.question: Which pronoun is used for 'We'?
questions.explanation: Hum (हम) translates directly to 'We'.

questions.question: Complete: ___ kahan ja rahe ho? (You)
questions.explanation: 'Tum' pairs with the verb ending 'ho'.

topics.title: Gender in Hindi (Masculine and Feminine)
topics.description: Understand grammatical gender for nouns and how it influences adjectives and verbs.

lesson.introduction: Every noun in Hindi is either masculine or feminine. Unlike English, Hindi gender affects verbs and adjectives.

points.title: Noun Endings & Gender Patterns
points.description: Many masculine nouns end with '-aa', while many feminine nouns end with '-ee'.

questions.question: What is the typical ending for many masculine nouns in Hindi?
questions.explanation: Many base masculine nouns terminate in an '-aa' sound.

questions.question: The feminine equivalent of 'ladka' (boy) is ___.
questions.explanation: Ladki is the feminine noun for girl.

questions.question: How many grammatical genders exist in standard Hindi?
questions.explanation: Hindi nouns are strictly divided into Masculine and Feminine.

questions.question: Complete: Beta lamba hai -> Beti ___ hai.
questions.explanation: Feminine noun 'beti' requires the feminine adjective form 'lambi'.

topics.title: Singular and Plural
topics.description: Learn how singular nouns transition to plural forms across different genders.

lesson.introduction: Turning singular nouns into plurals follows systematic rules in Hindi based on gender endings.

points.title: Masculine Plural Rule
points.description: Masculine nouns ending in '-aa' change to '-e' in the plural.

points.title: Feminine Plural Rule
points.description: Feminine nouns ending in '-ee' change to '-iyan' in the plural.

questions.question: What is the plural form of the masculine noun 'ladka' (boy)?
questions.explanation: Masculine nouns ending in '-aa' change to '-e' in the plural.

questions.question: The plural form of the feminine noun 'kitaab' (book) is ___.
questions.explanation: Consonant-ending feminine nouns add '-ein'.

questions.question: Which helping verb is used for plural subjects?
questions.explanation: 'Hain' (with nasalization) is the plural form of 'is/am'.

questions.question: Complete plural form: 'Kursi' (chair) becomes ___.
questions.explanation: Feminine '-ee' nouns pluralize by adding '-yan'.

topics.title: Demonstrative Pronouns (Yeh, Vah, Ye, Ve)
topics.description: Learn how to point to things using proximal and distal demonstrative pronouns.

lesson.introduction: Demonstrative pronouns let you point out people or objects. In Hindi, they double as 'this', 'that', 'these', 'those' as well as third-person pronouns.

points.title: Near vs Far Pointing
points.description: Yeh points to things close by; Vah points to things further away.

questions.question: Which word means 'This' or nearby 'He/She' in Hindi?
questions.explanation: 'Yeh' is the proximal demonstrative pronoun.

questions.question: The distal demonstrative pronoun meaning 'That' is ___.
questions.explanation: 'Vah' points to distant objects or people.

questions.question: What is the plural form of 'Yeh'?
questions.explanation: 'Ye' is the plural form of 'Yeh' (These).

questions.question: To point to multiple items far away, you use ___.
questions.explanation: 'Ve' translates to 'Those' or distant 'They'.

topics.title: Possessive Words (Mera, Meri, Mere)
topics.description: Learn how possessive adjectives agree in gender and number with the possessed object.

lesson.introduction: In Hindi, possessive words change based on the gender and number of the object being possessed, not the owner.

points.title: The 'My' Triad (Mera / Meri / Mere)
points.description: Mera (masculine singular), Meri (feminine singular/plural), Mere (masculine plural).

questions.question: Which possessive form is used with a masculine singular object?
questions.explanation: 'Mera' modifies masculine singular objects (e.g., mera ghar).

questions.question: For a feminine object like 'kitaab' (book), you use ___.
questions.explanation: 'Meri' is used for feminine objects regardless of the owner's gender.

questions.question: What determines whether you use 'mera', 'meri', or 'mere'?
options: The gender and number of the possessed object
questions.answer: The gender and number of the possessed object
questions.explanation: Possessive adjectives agree entirely with the item being possessed.

questions.question: Complete: Yeh ___ laptop hai. (My - masculine singular)
questions.explanation: 'Laptop' is masculine singular, taking 'mera'.

topics.title: Basic Helping Verbs (Hai, Hoon, Ho, Hain)
topics.description: Master the core auxiliary verbs used to express 'is', 'am', 'are' in Hindi.

lesson.introduction: Helping verbs complete basic sentences by linking subjects to descriptions or locations. They correspond directly to 'to be' verbs in English.

points.title: Conjugating Helping Verbs
points.description: Each pronoun pairs with a specific helping verb form.

questions.question: Which helping verb pairs exclusively with 'Main' (I)?
questions.explanation: 'Hoon' is the first-person singular auxiliary verb.

questions.question: The helping verb used for plural subjects and formal 'Aap' is ___.
questions.explanation: 'Hain' covers plurals and formal singular references.

questions.question: What is the correct helping verb for 'Tum'?
questions.explanation: 'Tum' always pairs with 'ho'.

questions.question: Complete: Tum kahan ___ ?
questions.explanation: 'Tum' pairs with 'ho'.

topics.title: Making Simple Affirmative Sentences
topics.description: Combine pronouns, nouns, adjectives, and helping verbs to build complete affirmative sentences.

lesson.introduction: Now that you have learned pronouns, gender, plurals, possessives, and helping verbs, you can combine them to build complete, natural affirmative sentences.

points.title: Putting It All Together
points.description: Subject + Object/Complement + Helping Verb structure in practice.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly translates 'My office is big'?
questions.explanation: 'Office' is masculine singular, taking 'mera' and 'bada'.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: Yeh meri ___ hai. (Car)
questions.explanation: 'Car' or 'gaadi' are feminine, taking 'meri'.

questions.question: What is the primary formula for building a basic affirmative sentence in Hindi?
questions.explanation: The fundamental SOV pattern rules all basic affirmative sentences.

questions.question: Complete: Main ek student ___ .
questions.explanation: 'Main' pairs with 'hoon'.
